candidate_sentence_map.S1: AB Pieno Žvaigždės reported a substantial improvement in profitability in the first three months of 2026, although revenue remained broadly stable.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Revenue was EUR 52.064 million, down slightly from EUR 52.324 million in the same period of 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Sales in Lithuania declined to EUR 31.405 million from EUR 32.112 million, while sales in other EU countries increased to EUR 11.341 million from EUR 10.801 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: By product group, fresh milk sales were almost unchanged, dry milk sales decreased, and cheese and other product sales increased.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: The main improvement came from a significant reduction in the cost of sales, which fell to EUR 38.078 million from EUR 42.530 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: As a result, gross profit increased 43% to EUR 13.986 million, compared with EUR 9.794 million a year earlier, and the gross margin improved from approximately 18.7% to 26.9%.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Other operating income also increased to EUR 363 thousand from EUR 28 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: These developments more than offset the 18% increase in sales and administrative expenses, which reached EUR 10.983 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Operating profit before finance costs consequently rose to EUR 3.366 million from EUR 535 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Net finance expenses improved slightly to EUR 298 thousand from EUR 308 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Profit before tax and net profit both reached EUR 3.068 million, compared with EUR 227 thousand in the first quarter of 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: EBITDA increased to EUR 4.730 million from EUR 2.001 million, while earnings per share rose to EUR 0.07 from EUR 0.01.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: No corporate income tax was recognized in the income statement for either period.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Net cash flow from operating activities turned positive at EUR 1.625 million, compared with an outflow of EUR 183 thousand in the prior-year period.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Cash flows from ordinary activities before working-capital changes increased to EUR 4.336 million from EUR 1.367 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Improved inventory-related cash flow supported the result, although receivables increased and used EUR 2.536 million of cash.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Investing outflows declined to EUR 551 thousand from EUR 1.058 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Financing activities resulted in a EUR 723 thousand outflow, compared with a EUR 4.133 million inflow a year earlier, when the company received EUR 8.5 million in loans.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Cash therefore increased from EUR 1.806 million at year-end 2025 to EUR 2.157 million, but remained below EUR 4.902 million at 31 March 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Total assets rose to EUR 85.305 million from EUR 83.475 million at year-end, while equity increased to EUR 41.164 million from EUR 38.238 million, mainly reflecting first-quarter profit.
candidate_sentence_map.S22: Total liabilities declined to EUR 44.141 million from EUR 45.237 million, and the current ratio improved to 1.51 from 1.27.
candidate_sentence_map.S23: No material post-balance-sheet events were reported.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: All HIGH items (K1-K5) are fully represented. K6 is only partially covered because the candidate reports a different operating-cash-flow figure (EUR 1.625 m vs. the required EUR 2.41 m). K8 and K9 are only partially covered because the candidate omits the required percentage shares and the explicit year-over-year comparison for dry-milk products. The overall picture of improved profitability and liquidity is captured.
